clue.text: Be resolute and reject pleas for disarmament

definitions.meaning: to hold firm and refuse to change one's position
read literally: a soldier refusing to give up their weapons keeps hold of them

explanation.surface: A defiant leader refuses calls to lay down arms and stands firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means refusing to yield an opinion, and literally describes keeping one's weapons rather than surrendering them.

parts.note: read 'Well one' as a healthy person: a state payment for the ill is something only the unwell can claim

explanation.surface: A remark about an allowance that is out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a sentence opener, but it means healthy: a person in good health cannot claim money paid to those off work through illness.
explanation.definitionFit: This British state payment went to people unable to work through illness, so a healthy person had no claim to it.

parts.note: suggests a craftsman carving ivory, but means a front tooth, itself made of ivory-like dentine, that cuts food

explanation.surface: A craftsman who carves elephant tusks.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are jokingly called ivories, and the front teeth are the ones that bite and slice food.

definitions.meaning: a type or variety, as in 'of that sort'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both benevolent in temperament and a class or category of things.

clue.text: Not an inside job at the remote settlement

definitions.meaning: read as a post (job) that is out, away from the centre
a frontier station far from the main base

explanation.surface: A crime story set in a distant colony, ruling out a culprit within.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlying base is a distant settlement, and split in two the word is a job located outside.

indicators.note: the letters of the two preceding words must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something certain to alter, without question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges BOUND TO into NO DOUBT; 'Bound' looks like a jump or an obligation but is simply anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases express certainty, as in 'he will come, surely'.

clue.text: One in bondage endlessly in Eastern Europe

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word for a bonded person is dropped

parts.note: a person held in bondage is a slave

explanation.surface: Someone held captive without end somewhere in the eastern part of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the last letter, E, from SLAVE. The definition is loose: a person found in Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavic peoples, such as Poles, Czechs and Russians, live mainly across the east of the continent.

clue.text: Howl when girl gets up to stir tea

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the girl's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lulu is a girl's name

indicators.note: stirring mixes up the letters of the drink's name

explanation.surface: Someone wails when a young woman rises to stir her cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' turns LULU into ULUL; 'to stir' shuffles TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail with a long high trembling cry, as mourners or wolves do.

parts.note: the flag of the United States, whose design shows heavenly emblems and bands

explanation.surface: A note on what the American flag displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' means a flag, and the States are the USA; the clue also says what that flag features.
explanation.definitionFit: The American national flag is nicknamed after its fifty white emblems and thirteen red and white bands.

parts.note: suggests a suitable goal for timid people, but a shy is a stall at a funfair where balls are thrown

explanation.surface: Advice about whom bashful people should aim for.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw wooden balls to knock nuts off posts; 'shy' is a throw, not timidity.
explanation.definitionFit: These hairy nuts are the prizes knocked off stands at fairground throwing stalls.

parts.note: looks like a medical test, but means a nobleman who feeds on blood

explanation.surface: A hospital test measuring cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire is a Transylvanian count who drinks blood.

clue.text: Presumably where one get's a flight home

definitions.text: Presumably where one get's a flight home

parts.words: Presumably where one get's a flight home
parts.note: suggests an airport, but a young bird's home is where it takes its first flight

explanation.surface: A traveller's guess at where to catch a plane back.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in "get's" is as printed. A fledgling bird flies from its home, so its 'flight home' is the place it was raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build these homes and fledglings leave them on their first flights.

clue.text: Additional payment that is good in France and America

parts.note: bon is the French word for good
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A bonus sounds good whether you are paid in Paris or New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid on top of normal wages, such as a year-end reward.

parts.note: Ma's, ma being an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother attends a second church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of MA'S is ignored in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist celebrated in the Catholic church is a religious service.

clue.text: The country where father is in January

indicators.note: the word for dad sits within the month's abbreviation

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Asking which land Dad is visiting at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation in East Asia.

clue.text: Tactless remark the boss almost makes

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: The manager nearly always makes indiscreet comments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter, R, from GAFFER, the British informal word for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: A social blunder, especially a clumsy indiscreet comment.

clue.text: One paid to work in tavern's restoration

indicators.note: rebuilding the pub's name means putting its letters into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A hired hand employed in refurbishing a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration' rearranges TAVERNS, the S of the possessive counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic employee who is hired to carry out work for a household.

parts.note: trade means commerce or business
the printed 'available' split in transcription; in means available, as in fruit being in season

explanation.surface: A commercial deal where an old item can be handed over towards a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: IN can mean available or obtainable, as in 'strawberries are in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving an old car or appliance as partial payment for a new one is this kind of deal.

clue.text: One of the herd in New York state

definitions.meaning: a bison, an animal that lives in herds
a city in western New York, near Niagara Falls

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a large wild ox of the plains and a city in upstate New York.

indicators.note: suggests the letters might form another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: Something frail? Possibly that description fits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' shuffles EGFRAIL into the answer, and the whole clue also defines it: frail is an example of delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily broken or delicate, the same quality as being frail.

parts.note: taken as written
wards are rooms for patients in a hospital

explanation.surface: Moving ahead in this way through the hospital rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means forward, describing movement ahead.

parts.note: RE is the school subject abbreviation
forms are school classes in Britain

explanation.surface: Changes for the better in school religion lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class of pupils, and RE is religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Changes that make a system better are improvements.

clue.text: Its root made into an Italian dish

indicators.note: the letters are made into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A root vegetable cooked into a meal from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made into' rearranges ITS ROOT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

definitions.meaning: a professional member of the standing army
even or consistent, as in a steady pace

explanation.surface: A serviceman wearing his kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a full-time professional soldier and also means even or unvarying.

clue.text: The first man to apply a double entry system?

definitions.text: The first man to apply a double entry system?

parts.words: The first man to apply a double entry system?
parts.note: suggests a pioneer of bookkeeping, but means the ark-builder who let animals in two by two

explanation.surface: A question about who invented double-entry bookkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch took animals onto his ark in pairs.

definitions.meaning: a ... roll is a rolled sponge cake

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone from Switzerland and, in Britain, a jam-filled rolled sponge cake.

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Offering a choice between a fish and seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly extracted from red seaweeds, used in labs and cooking, and the term also loosely names the weed.

indicators.note: turning the little word round means its letters are written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone to rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the first TO into OT, then the second TO follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's name.

parts.note: to means until, as in nine to five
1 is the Roman numeral I and 50 is the Roman numeral L

explanation.surface: Labour hard right up to ten to two.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1.50 not as a time but as two Roman numerals, I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour or slog with great effort.

definitions.meaning: a piece of fruit or meat fried in batter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to waste time or money bit by bit, and also a battered fried snack.

clue.text: Some soldiers accept 2 from the slattern

indicators.note: the group of soldiers takes the other letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: a troop is a group of soldiers
two of the letter L; the pound sign before the 2 has probably been lost in transcription, L being the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: Some soldiers take money from a slovenly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accept' puts LL inside TROOP. Two pounds is LL, from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are dated insults for an untidy or promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Where members are entitled to sit

definitions.text: Where members are entitled to sit

parts.words: Where members are entitled to sit
parts.note: suggests a right to a seat, but means a chamber whose members hold titles

explanation.surface: A statement about which members have a right to a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' means both having a right and having a title: peers sit in the upper chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper chamber of the UK Parliament, whose members are peers holding titles.
